subject: Your parcel needs a new delivery address
preview: The final delivery attempt could not be completed.
preheader: Address confirmation is needed before tonight.
heroCaption: Parcel SB-4182 is waiting at the depot
bodyParagraphs: We could not match the entrance details for parcel SB-4182.
Update the delivery address by 8:00 PM or the parcel will be returned.
smsBody: SwiftBox: Parcel SB-4182 needs an address update by 8 PM. Update now:

clues.label: A deadline tonight
clues.detail: "By 8:00 PM or the parcel will be returned" is there to rush you past checking.

clues.label: A parcel you weren't expecting
clues.detail: Ask yourself: did I order something? The shop's own app or site shows real tracking.

clues.label: It asks for personal details
clues.detail: Updating an address from a surprise link hands your details to whoever sent it.

lesson: Delivery deadlines are there to rush you.
Check an expected order in the site you normally use.
Avoid updating personal details from a surprise link.

subject: Unusual transfer paused for review
preheader: Review unusual activity before access is limited.
heroCaption: Outgoing transfer of $684.20 is on hold
bodyParagraphs: A $684.20 transfer from your household account was paused after an unusual sign-in.
Confirm whether you recognize it before outgoing transfers are locked.

clues.label: Fear about your money
clues.detail: A scary dollar amount makes people act before they think.

clues.label: "Before transfers are locked"
clues.detail: Threats of losing access are a common pressure tactic.

clues.label: There's a safer way to check
clues.detail: Open your bank's app yourself, or call the number on the back of your card.

lesson: Money alerts trigger urgency and fear.
Open your known account app rather than this link.
Contact support using a trusted statement or card.

subject: Your family plan renewal was declined
preheader: Your latest family plan receipt needs attention.
heroCaption: Your family plan pauses at midnight
bodyParagraphs: The renewal below could not be completed.
Update billing before midnight to keep profiles and watchlists active.

clues.label: A midnight cutoff
clues.detail: Losing your shows tonight is meant to make the click feel urgent.

clues.label: An odd "retry fee"
clues.detail: Scammers often add a small, unexpected fee. Real services rarely charge to retry a card.

clues.label: Billing from a link
clues.detail: Check billing in the app you already use, never from an email button.

lesson: Subscription interruptions can provoke a quick click.
Check billing from the app you already use.
Question unexpected fees and deadlines.

subject: Threats found on a family computer
preview: Isolation is required to protect shared files.
preheader: Three threats may spread to shared devices.
heroCaption: Shared family files may be at risk
bodyParagraphs: A recent scan found three threats that may access shared family files.
Start isolation now before other home devices are affected.

clues.label: Alarming language
clues.detail: Scammers pick words like "threats found" and "spread" to make you panic.

clues.label: Security software doesn't email you scans
clues.detail: Real antivirus warnings appear on the device itself, not in your inbox.

clues.label: The next step is usually remote access
clues.detail: Tech-support scams end with "let us connect to your computer". Never allow it from a surprise message.

lesson: Virus warnings use alarming language.
Do not grant remote access from an unexpected notice.
Run security tools directly from your device settings.

subject: Field trip permission is still missing
preview: Your child's place may be released this afternoon.
preheader: Permission and activity fee are due today.
bodyParagraphs: The permission record for next week's science center visit is incomplete.
Complete it by 3:30 PM so your child's place is not released.

clues.label: It's about your child
clues.detail: Worry about your kids makes it hard to slow down. That's why scammers use it.

clues.label: A same-day deadline and a fee
clues.detail: Pay by 3:30 PM or lose the spot. Pressure plus payment is a red flag.

clues.label: A sign-in page from a link
clues.detail: Go to the school portal the way you normally do, or call the school office.

lesson: Messages about children make it hard to slow down.
Use the school contact details you already know.
Confirm sudden fees and deadlines separately.

subject: Your wallet access will be locked
heroCaption: Verify within 30 minutes to keep access
bodyParagraphs: A new device attempted to open your household wallet from another city.
Verify the activity within 30 minutes or access will be locked.
smsBody: PayNest: New device activity may lock your wallet. Review:

clues.label: A 30-minute countdown
clues.detail: Tight countdowns leave no time to check, which is the point.

clues.label: "Verify" means "type your password"
clues.detail: The link leads to a sign-in page. Real alerts never need you to sign in from an email.

clues.label: Check it yourself
clues.detail: Open the app directly and look at recent activity there.

lesson: Lockout threats create artificial urgency.
Open the known service directly to review activity.
Never enter account details after following a surprise link.

subject: A small parcel fee is holding your delivery
preview: Clear the balance before the return window.
heroCaption: Parcel SB-9031 is held at the local depot
bodyParagraphs: Parcel SB-9031 has reached the local depot with a $2.40 sorting balance.
Clear it today to prevent return processing.

clues.label: A tiny amount
clues.detail: $2.40 feels harmless. The real goal is your card number.

clues.label: Fees to release a parcel
clues.detail: Couriers rarely ask for surprise fees by email. Check with the shop you ordered from.

clues.label: Payment through a link
clues.detail: Never pay from a link in a message you weren't expecting.

lesson: Small charges can feel harmless.
Verify parcel references against real orders.
Do not pay through unexpected links.

subject: Receipt for a payment you may not recognize
preview: Report this payment before it settles.
bodyParagraphs: This payment is scheduled to settle later today.
If nobody in your household made it, review the invoice now.

clues.label: A purchase you didn't make
clues.detail: Fake receipts make you want to "cancel" fast. That urge is what the scammer wants.

clues.label: "Before it settles"
clues.detail: This is another deadline. You can still dispute a real charge later through your own account.

clues.label: Look at your real history
clues.detail: Open the payment app or bank you use and check there.

lesson: An unfamiliar purchase can trigger panic.
Check transaction history through a known app.
Ask household members before disputing a charge.

subject: Unpaid toll balance: final notice
preview: Avoid a $25 late fee by paying today.
preheader: Your vehicle passed a toll point without a valid pass.
bodyParagraphs: Our records show an unpaid toll of $4.15 from a recent trip on the Crestway corridor.
Pay today to avoid a $25.00 late fee and a hold on your vehicle registration.
smsBody: Crestway Tolls: You have an unpaid toll of $4.15. Pay today to avoid a $25 late fee:

clues.label: Did you even drive a toll road?
clues.detail: Unpaid-toll texts and emails are one of the most common scams right now. Most go to people who never used that road.

clues.label: Small fee, big threat
clues.detail: It asks for $4.15 now or threatens $25 and a registration hold. Growing threats push you to pay fast.

clues.label: Pay only through a site you type in
clues.detail: If you think you owe a toll, go to the toll agency's website yourself.

lesson: Unpaid-toll messages are a top scam right now.
A small amount is a way to get your card number.
Check tolls by typing the agency's site yourself.

subject: Your photos will be deleted in 48 hours
preview: Your storage is full and backups have stopped.
preheader: 2,418 photos and videos are scheduled for removal.
bodyParagraphs: Your storage plan is full and new photos are no longer backed up.
Upgrade now to keep your library. Photos over the limit will be removed in 48 hours.

clues.label: Threatening your memories
clues.detail: Losing family photos is a real fear, and scammers use it.

clues.label: "Deleted in 48 hours"
clues.detail: Real storage services warn you for weeks and never delete photos on short notice.

clues.label: Check storage in your settings
clues.detail: Your phone's settings show how much storage you use. You don't need a link.

lesson: Scammers threaten family photos to scare you.
Real services don't delete your files on short notice.
Check storage in your device settings, not from a link.

subject: A document was shared with you: "Updated household invoice"
preview: Sign in to view the shared file.
preheader: You have 1 new shared document waiting.
bodyParagraphs: The Accounts Team shared a document with you.
For your security, sign in to view the file. This link expires in 24 hours.

clues.label: Shared by someone you don't know
clues.detail: "The Accounts Team" could be anyone. Who sent this?

clues.label: A sign-in page to view a file
clues.detail: Fake sign-in pages are a common way scammers steal passwords. The page looks real and records what you type.

clues.label: Ask the sender another way
clues.detail: If you think someone did share a file, text or call them to check.

lesson: Fake shared files often lead to stolen passwords.
Be suspicious of any sign-in page you reached from a link.
Confirm with the sender another way before opening.
